articles.title: Peace only way for Manipur to participate in India''s development journey: CM
articles.description: Imphal, Oct 17 (PTI): Manipur Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh on Saturday said peace is the only way for the ethnic strife-torn state to participate in the country's journey of development. His comment came on a day when a man was shot dead and four others were injured in a gun attack by suspected militants in Kamjong district. Addressing a programme - Jan Sevak Mahakumbh - here, the chief minister said India cannot be considered a developed country without the development of Manipur. "Peace is the only way for the state to participate in the journey of development," he said. The ethnic conflict that erupted in May 2023 between the Imphal valley-based Meitei and hill-based Kuki communities has claimed at least 306 lives, while 49 people remain missing and thousands have been left homeless. In recent months, clashes between Kuki and Naga communities have also been reported. State Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam stated that restoring peace in Manipur requires mutual trust and understanding among all communities. Addressing the Jan Sevak Mahakumbh here, the chief minister said the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' has been observed across all districts of Manipur from September 17 to October 17 to mark the 25 years of public service rendered by Narendra Modi as Gujarat chief minister and then as the prime minister. "The successful month-long campaign witnessed the participation of more than 4 lakh people in 6,122 venues across the state," Singh added. The CM said the Manipuri language serves as a medium of communication among all communities in the state and emphasised the need to cherish the language and encourage its wider use among the people. Under the leadership of the prime minister, the vision of 'Viksit Bharat' 2047 is to build a strong India by the time the country attains 100 years of independence, he said. Referring to the public demand for the updation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC) before the Census, Singh said the Centre has been informed about the concerns raised by the people of Manipur and has deferred the Census exercise in the state. articles.title: World News: Indian Diaspora in London Backs PM Modi Outside Indian High Commission
articles.description: Amid heightened political tensions in Delhi, members of the Indian diaspora gathered outside the Indian High Commission in London to express their support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The gathering featured slogans in support of Modi, India, and national pride, including chants of “Jai Shri Ram” and “Bharat Mata Ki Jai.” According to the report, the demonstration took place in response to protests organized by the BJP and Congress in Delhi. Participants at the London gathering voiced their concerns over what they described as attempts to damage India's reputation internationally through political criticism. The demonstrators argued that India is a democracy where citizens have access to legal remedies, including approaching courts and the Supreme Court, if they have grievances. They questioned why political disputes should be taken overseas and expressed the view that allegations should be supported by evidence. The gathering brought together members of the Indian community who wanted to publicly demonstrate their support for the prime minister and the country's development. Slogans such as “Modi Modi” and “Jai Bharat Mata Ki” echoed during the event, reflecting the participants' patriotic sentiments and political views. The development highlights how political debates within India can extend beyond national borders, prompting members of the Indian diaspora to organize demonstrations and express their opinions in international cities. London, home to a large Indian-origin community, has frequently served as a venue for public gatherings related to Indian political and social issues. The event also underscores the contrasting narratives surrounding political protests, national image, and democratic expression. The demonstrators' statements represent the views expressed by participants at the gathering.

articles.title: Political News: BJP Targets Opposition Over Tiranga Yatra, Claims Protest Failed to Draw Crowd
articles.description: The political debate surrounding the Tiranga Yatra has intensified after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) launched a sharp attack on the opposition over its alleged attempt to organize the march. According to the BJP, the initiative, reportedly undertaken at the direction of opposition leaders, failed to attract a significant number of participants, turning the effort into a political setback. Taking a sarcastic swipe at Rajiv, the speaker suggested that the situation would have been embarrassing, arguing that even a small gathering could not be mobilized. The remarks questioned the opposition's ability to demonstrate public support and raised doubts about its approach to organizing protests. The speaker further alleged that opposition leaders prefer holding protests at selected locations because such events can generate publicity without requiring substantial organizational effort or attracting a large crowd. To underline the criticism, the speaker used a popular Hindi proverb, implying that some political actors seek recognition and impressive results without putting in the necessary work. The comments add another layer to the ongoing political confrontation between the BJP and opposition parties over public demonstrations, political messaging, and the symbolism associated with the national flag. The Tiranga Yatra, which carries patriotic significance, has become the focus of competing political narratives, with both sides likely to interpret participation and public response differently. While the BJP has portrayed the reported turnout as evidence of an unsuccessful political mobilization, the broader implications depend on the circumstances surrounding the event and the responses of the opposition leaders involved. The exchange highlights how public rallies and protest campaigns continue to serve as important platforms for political messaging and criticism in India's evolving political landscape.
